info.title: OpenAsy DAST API
info.summary: Findings from scans of running applications, on targets whose owner has proven they own them.
info.description:
Every screen of dast uses this API, and so can your scripts and CI (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Send SARIF 2.1.0 reports from ZAP, Nuclei or another scanner with `DAST_INGEST_TOKEN`. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.description:
Takes a SARIF 2.1.0 report from ZAP, Nuclei or another scanner of running applications, for a target that exists. Findings outside the target's address are left out. What the same engine reported before and does not report now is fixed. The first report of an engine adopts what is there; later ones fail the check for new findings at or above the target's `failOn`.

```bash
nuclei -u https://shop.example.com -se results.sarif
curl -sf -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $DAST_INGEST_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @results.sarif \
  "https://dast.example.com/api/v1/scans?target=shop-staging" | tee scan.json
test "$(jq .passed scan.json)" = true
```

The body may be gzipped (`Content-Encoding: gzip`), up to 64 MiB unpacked, with at most 20,000 results.

Takes DAST_INGEST_TOKEN, or an API token with the editor role.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: Which engine made the report. Without it, the first word of the tool's name in lowercase, such as `zap` or `nuclei`. Reports of one engine replace each other; engines do not fix each other's findings.

201.description: Compared with what the engine reported before. `passed` says whether the check passes.

post.description:
An address that may be tested. Nothing is attacked until its owner has proven it is theirs (ADR 0037).

Needs the admin role.

201.description: Created, not yet verified. Serve `verification.content` at `verification.url`, then ask for verification.

patch.description:
Marks it as production, which never gets a full scan without an admin's say, and sets the severity that fails a check.

Needs the admin role.

delete.description:
Deletes its reports, findings and decisions.

Needs the admin role.

post.description:
Fetches `/.well-known/openasy-dast` from the target's origin over the public internet, without following redirects, and compares it with the verification content. Addresses on private networks are refused: an agent in that network verifies them.

Needs the admin role.

A target on a private address is read by an enrolled dast-agent in its network instead: the answer is then 422 saying so, a verify job waits in the queue, and the target is verified once the agent has read the proof.

Queues a scan of the target for dast-agent. A target that is not verified gets only a passive scan; asking for more is 409. A full scan of a production target needs an admin; an editor gets 403. One waiting scan per target: asking again changes its profile.

Needs the editor role.

get.description: Without their secrets, so anyone who starts scans can pick one.

post.description: The secret, a header value or a password, is sealed with openasy-kek, never sent back, and given only to the agent running a scan that uses it. ZAP uses both kinds; Nuclei sends a header login, and runs without a form login. 503 without openasy-kek. Needs the admin role.

delete.description: Scans that used it keep their findings. Needs the admin role.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` (default): reported by its engine and not triaged. `suppressed`: triaged and still reported. `resolved`: no longer reported.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches the rule, address or message.

put.description:
Marks a finding as a false positive or accepted risk, with a reason, or opens it again. The decision stays with the finding across reports.

Needs the editor role.

parameters.name: fingerprint
parameters.description: From a finding or a report.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` (default): reported by its engine and not triaged. `suppressed`: triaged and still reported. `resolved`: no longer reported.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches the rule, address or message.

200.description: From OPENASY_PRODUCTS, for the product switcher.
Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

get.description: The latest 200 scan and verify jobs, newest first; `target` narrows them to one target's id. A job an agent took and did not finish goes back to the queue, three times at most.

post.description: Returns a one-time enrolment token, valid for 7 days and shown once, for DAST_ENROLL_TOKEN of the new dast-agent. Needs the admin role.

delete.description: Its secret stops working. Needs the admin role.

post.description: Trades the one-time token for the agent's own secret.
The next job, leased to this agent for 3 hours, with the address and the profile the target allows now.
The SARIF of one engine for a running scan job. Reports are kept per engine and profile, such as zap-standard, so a passive scan never fixes what an active one found.

201.description: Compared with what the engine reported before. `passed` says whether the check passes.

post.description: Why the scan or the verification could not finish.
What the agent read at the target's proof address. The target is verified when it is the target's content; otherwise the job fails.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when dast runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the dast origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_dast_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when dast is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

ingestToken.description: `DAST_INGEST_TOKEN`: for CI. It can send scans, nothing else.

agentSecret.description: The secret a dast-agent got when it enrolled (oda_...).

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

FailOn.description: The lowest severity of a new finding that fails the check; `none` never fails it.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

active.description: False once the acceptance has expired; the finding is open again.

expiresAt.description: Required for accepted, at most 366 days away; optional for a false positive.

verified.description: Targets whose owner has proven the address is theirs.

failingChecks.description: Reports of the last 7 days that failed their check.

url.description: Origin and path; findings outside it are left out.

content.description: Serve exactly this text at url, then ask for verification.

nextScanAt.description: When the schedule queues the next scan.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

fingerprint.description: The same on every scan: rule, page without query string, parameter.

evidence.description: What the engine saw, with credentials masked.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

new.description: Findings the engine did not report before and nobody has triaged.

resolved.description: Findings this engine reported before and does not now.

ignored.description: Results outside the target's address, or without a web address.

blocking.description: New findings at or above failOn. Always 0 for the first report of an engine, which adopts what is there.

findings.description: The new findings, most severe first, up to 100.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

Profile.description: passive: ZAP crawls and only watches, sending no attacks. standard: ZAP's active rules at low strength and Nuclei's templates that are not intrusive. full: every rule of both, at medium strength.

authProfile.description: The login the scan used, by name.
The id of one of the target's logins, for a scan behind its sign-in page.

secret.description: The agent's own secret; only its hash is kept.

proofUrl.description: For verify: where the proof is.

auth.description: The login, with its secret, for this job only.

AuthProfile.description: How a scan gets past the target's login. The secret is never sent back.

NewAuthProfile.description: header: headerName and value, sent with every request. form: loginUrl on the target's origin, usernameField, passwordField, username, password, and loggedInRegex, a pattern only a signed-in page contains.
